deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1847 student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation', published posthumously in Riemann's Werke (1876). Notation: Π(s)=Γ(s+1). Formula (1) of the essay defines, for ν<0, ∂_x^ν φ = 1/Π(-ν-1) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} φ(t) dt + C_ν. Changing the base point k is absorbed into the complementary function C_ν. Other orders are reached through ∂^{ν+1} z = d(∂^ν z)/dx. The previous page treated φ = x^μ with μ>0 and found ∂^ν x^μ = Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν}. This page treats μ<0.

(a) For μ<0, x^μ is singular only at x=0. So in (1) the base point k must have the same sign as x, and one may not simply put k=0.

(b) Integrate by parts m times. At each step t^{μ+j} is integrated and (x-t)^{-ν-j} is differentiated. One step gives
∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt = [(x-t)^{-ν-1} t^{μ+1}/(μ+1)]_k^x + (-ν-1)/(μ+1) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-2} t^{μ+1} dt.
- The boundary term at t=x vanishes as long as the (x-t) exponent stays positive.
- The term at t=k has the form const·(x-k)^{-ν-j}, which belongs to C_ν. (These two points are my filling.)

After m steps the coefficients multiply to ∏_{j=1}^m (-ν-j)/(μ+j) = [Π(-ν-1)/Π(-ν-1-m)]·[Π(μ)/Π(μ+m)]. Hence
1/Π(-ν-1) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt = Π(μ)/(Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1-m} t^{μ+m} dt + C_ν.
This is valid as long as -ν-m>0.

(c) The aim is to raise the t-exponent above -1. One needs an integer m with -1-μ < m < -ν. Such an m exists when -ν>-μ (i.e. ν<μ), since the interval then has length >1. So integrals with μ<-1 are reduced to ones whose t-exponent μ+m exceeds -1.

(d) Once μ+m>-1, the piece ∫_0^k (x-t)^{-ν-1-m} t^{μ+m} dt is finite and belongs to C_ν. So the lower limit k may be replaced by 0. The Euler Beta integral then gives
Π(μ)/(Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m)) ∫_0^x (x-t)^{-ν-1-m} t^{μ+m} dt
= Π(μ)/(Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m)) · x^{μ-ν} Γ(-ν-m)Γ(μ+m+1)/Γ(μ-ν+1)
= Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν}.
Thus this is a value of ∂_x^ν(x^μ) whenever -ν>-μ.

(e) Since d/dx[Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν}] = Π(μ)/Π(μ-ν-1) x^{μ-ν-1}, the rule ∂^{ν+1} z = d∂^ν z/dx extends the formula to every ν.

(f) The page closes by announcing the exceptional case μ+m=-1, i.e. μ a negative integer, where Π(μ) is infinite. That case is treated on the next page and produces log x and Ψ (digamma) terms.

The red-pencil marginalia are a later editor's notation changes (𝔇 / ∂ for the derivative symbol) and 'besondere Zeile' typesetting instructions.
errors: Possible slip in the first display: the first factor of the denominator appears written as Π(-ν-1-m) with the '1' struck, i.e. Π(-ν-m). The correct value is Π(-ν-1-m), as Riemann himself writes in the following lines.
The integrand was first written as (x+t) and corrected to (x-t); the corrected version is right.

Not an error, but unstated: the boundary terms at t=k from each partial integration are silently absorbed into C_ν. Also, the condition for the boundary term at t=x to vanish is that the (x-t) exponent stay positive at each step, i.e. -ν-m>0. Riemann states this condition correctly after striking a μ.

Only a partial argument, not an error: the condition 'ν<μ' guarantees an integer m in (-1-μ, -ν). Riemann's phrase that the exponent of t becomes '≷ -1' should read '> -1'. The boundary case μ+m=-1 is deferred to the next page.

results.what: Reduction by m-fold integration by parts of the fractional integral of t^μ (μ<0) to one with t-exponent > -1, with the coefficient Π(μ)/(Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m))
results.modern_name: Integration by parts for the Riemann–Liouville integral / analytic continuation of the power rule

results.what: D^ν x^μ = Γ(μ+1)/Γ(μ-ν+1) x^{μ-ν} for negative non-integer μ (via Beta integral and the rule ∂^{ν+1}=d/dx ∂^ν)
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative/integral of a power function

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of Riemann's 1847 student essay on fractional differentiation, published in his Werke in 1876 and the origin of the name 'Riemann–Liouville'. The power-function formula and the partial-integration reduction are standard and already known as his.

transcription_corrections: In the first display the integrand reads (x±t) with the sign corrected to minus: (x-t)^{-ν-1}.
In the first display the denominator should be Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m); the struck symbol is a correction, and the intended (and later used) value is -ν-1-m.
'der Exponent von t ≷ -1 ist' should read 'der Exponent von t > -1 ist'.
'Nun erhält man aber durch m malige partielle Integration' — the m is a variable (m-malige), consistent with the formula.
The isolated expression 'Π(μ)/(Π(-ν-1-m)Π(μ+m))' at the end of the paragraph is partly struck in the image and simply restarts as the coefficient of the next displayed line.
The red marginalia are a later editorial hand: notation changes 𝔇_x^ν(x^μ) → ∂_x^ν(x^μ), and 'besondere Zeile' (set as separate line) beneath the coefficient.
